findings.title: Referer-only host check is spoofable and is also fragile
findings.body: `ensure_embeddable` trusts the `Referer` header to authorize embedding. The header is client-controlled, so non-browser clients can forge it. Browsers that send no Referer, because of privacy settings or an HTTPS to HTTP transition, are always rejected. Only the host is compared, so any page on the embeddable host, including user-generated content there, can embed. `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is also set on the response.

findings.title: Unescaped referer injected into inline JavaScript string
findings.body: `request.referer` is written into a single-quoted JS string with ERB's HTML escaping. HTML escaping does not escape a backslash, and a `<` becomes `<`, which is wrong inside a script block. The result is a broken `targetOrigin` and a possible script-injection vector. The value is also a full URL with a path, not an origin, so `postMessage` may not match the parent origin and the resize message may never be delivered. Use `escape_javascript`, or send only the origin.

findings.title: Weak origin check on received messages
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test. An empty origin, or an origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`, passes. It should be an exact comparison against the origin of `discourseUrl`.

findings.title: Kernel#open on a configurable URL; also unsafe content handling
findings.body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open` through open-uri. A value starting with `|` or a `file:` style path can read local files or run commands. The content is then stored as raw HTML (`raw_html` cook method) and rendered with `raw`, so imported feed content is not sanitized and becomes stored XSS.

findings.title: Feed item content can be nil, and String#scrub may be unavailable
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no `content` element, because many feeds only provide `description`. One bad item aborts the whole poll. `String#scrub` also requires Ruby 2.1.

findings.title: Mutates the caller's string and breaks change detection
findings.body: `contents <<` appends the footer in place. This mutates the caller's string, and it also fails on frozen strings. The footer is built from an unescaped `url`. `import_remote` fetches with `open(url)`, which has the same Kernel#open and SSRF problem.

findings.title: SSRF and local file access via open(url) in import_remote
findings.body: `open(url).read` is called without `require 'open-uri'`, so it may fall back to `Kernel#open` on a local path. `TopicRetriever` does check the host, but `import_remote` is also called directly from the thor task.

findings.title: Non-atomic setnx plus expire
findings.body: If the process dies between `setnx` and `expire`, the key never expires and the URL is permanently throttled. Use `set` with `ex` and `nx` instead.

findings.title: Test expects TopicRetriever.new but the controller enqueues a job
findings.body: The controller calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and never calls `TopicRetriever.new`. With jobs not run inline in tests, the `expects(:new)` expectations will fail.
